subject: SP role lifecycle, subprocessor notice window, and interstate dataflow evidence
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@brightlinehealth.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.example
Cc: Brightline Legal <legal@brightlinehealth.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Vendor evidence request: subprocessor lifecycle + interstate transfer mapping

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the demo last week. As part of our procurement review and the US-state privacy annex, legal asked us to get a few concrete artifacts from Redwood before we finalize the DPA. Can you provide evidence and/or commitments for the following?

1) Subprocessor lifecycle: the onboarding/offboarding process, notice windows to customers when a new subprocessor is added, and the maximum time a subprocessor may have access to telemetry/production logs.
2) Interstate dataflow mapping: proof of how health telemetry is routed, specifically any instances where telemetry may transit out of-state and whether onshore fallback is available.
3) Addendum language: a suggested clause we can use for Brightline's US-state privacy addendum that clarifies Redwood's role (service provider vs sale) and handles emergency subprocessors.

We created a short RFI PDF attached with requested formats. Ideally we need these artifacts by EOD Monday to keep our review on track. If any of this is sensitive, please indicate an objection and we can handle via an NDA or redline process.

Appreciate it —
Maria
Director, Vendor Risk
Brightline Health
[Attachment: Brightline_RFI_Subprocessors_11282026.pdf (PDF)]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.example>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@brightlinehealth.com>
Cc: Brightline Legal <legal@brightlinehealth.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Vendor evidence request: subprocessor lifecycle + interstate transfer mapping

Hi Maria —

Thanks, and great to hear the demo was useful. Attaching a concise set of artifacts to start: (1) our current subprocessor register export, (2) a short operations note about onboarding/offboarding windows, and (3) a draft DPA addendum suggested for US-state annexes.

Quick answers up front:
- Notice window: standard is 30 days for routine additions. For emergency or security-critical subprocessors (on-call failover, short-term capacity), we provide as much notice as possible and post a notice in the Console within 24–72 hours; we also offer an onshore fallback plan for regulated accounts where required.
- Access duration: telemetry/production logs access for third-party subprocessors is time-limited and scoped by purpose; typical access duration is 14–90 days depending on purpose (incident remediation vs ongoing analytics). We can provide per-subprocessor access windows in the exported register.
- Interstate routing: our Smart Routing layer may route requests across regions for cost/latency, but for regulated customers we can pin routes to onshore capacity and provide a documented fallback. The attached dataflow note shows default paths and onshore fallback controls.

Attachments included: redwood-subprocessors-202611.xlsx (filtered export), redwood-dpa-usstate-proposal-20261128.docx, and a short operations note. If Brightline needs SOC2 artifact mappings, we can coordinate with Security for a narrow scope review.

Happy to walk through the DPA language — propose a call Monday 11/30 at 11am PT if that works.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.example>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.example>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@ben_carter@redwood.example>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 11:42:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: SP vs operator nuance and proposed emergency-subprocessor language

Grace —

Quick internal note before we respond to Brightline's legal team in detail:

1) Classification: we should be explicit that Redwood is a "service provider / processor" under CPRA/CCPA/US-state annexes — not a reseller/operator — but acknowledge limited operator-like activities for certain telemetry routing (e.g., anonymized analytics we run for platform quality). Avoid language that implies sale or independent use.

2) Emergency subprocessors: propose the following brightline-friendly clause (draft):
"In the event Redwood requires an emergency third-party engagement to restore services or respond to a security incident, Redwood will: (a) in good faith select subprocessors bound by equivalent contractual obligations; (b) notify Customer within 24–72 hours with scope and duration; and (c) offer an onshore fallback or mitigations where Customer can demonstrate material regulatory constraints."

3) Notice window trade-offs: 30 days for routine additions is standard; we can offer a shorter 14-day advance notice for Brightline as a negotiated term, with the caveat that emergency additions remain post-facto notice.

4) Evidence: include per-subprocessor access logs and time-bound access attestations. Security can generate an export of access windows for the last 12 months. I'd flag any subprocessors that have transient access longer than 90 days for review.

I'll draft a redline for the addendum doc and hand to Legal next. Ben — can you validate the access-window exports are straightforward? Karthik — any notes on the routing/onshore fallback doc?

— Olga

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.example>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@brightlinehealth.com>
Cc: Brightline Legal <legal@brightlinehealth.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.example>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 13:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Vendor evidence request: subprocessor lifecycle + interstate transfer mapping

Maria —

Appreciate the RFI; below is a short package and next steps and we've attached the DPA addendum language for your counsel to consider (redwood-dpa-usstate-proposal-20261128.docx). Key points and commitments we can sign to in the addendum: 

- Role: Redwood confirms we act as a Service Provider/Processor; we do not perform sales-making uses of Customer personal data.
- Routine notice: 30-day advance notice for routine subprocessor additions; for Brightline we can contractually shorten to 14 days.
- Emergency subprocessors: Redwood will notify Brightline within 24–72 hours, supply scope/duration, and offer onshore mitigation where feasible as described in the draft clause.
- Access windows: We will provide per-subprocessor access-window attestations and a CSV export showing access start/end and purpose; typical ranges: 14–90 days.
- Interstate routing: Default routing may cross state boundaries for latency/cost; for regulated customers we can provide onshore-only routing and an operational fallback with documented SLA impact.

Requested deliverables and timing:
- Today: exported subprocessor register (attached) + draft addendum (attached) + dataflow diagram link.
- Monday 11/30 EOD: per-subprocessor access-window export (Security produces CSV) + suggested redlines from Brightline Legal.
- If Brightline requests an operational onshore-only pinning configuration, we will provide a configuration runbook and estimated cost impact by 12/07.

If Monday 11/30 11am PT works, we'll go over the addendum language and the export format. If you'd prefer Legal-only call, we can do that too.

Thanks —
Grace
